invest.small: Scoped to routing + API surface only; zone-internal logic is out of scope for this story.

sprint_1_stories.persona: Host AI system integrator embedding Dashanan as a library or sidecar

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a host calls the unified context-assembly API, When the request does not name any individual zone, Then the Orchestrator resolves and returns assembled context sourced from the correct zones without the host needing zone-level knowledge.

Given the Orchestrator is called before any zone story lands, When a routing request targets an unimplemented zone, Then the facade returns a typed 'zone not available' response rather than an unhandled error, so later zone stories can register without a facade contract change.

sprint_2_stories.title: Zone 3 Semantic Memory store - SemanticEdge and GeneralFact schema with non-duplication CHECK constraint
sprint_2_stories.hld_citation: HLD Section 3.4 (owned entities SemanticEdge, GeneralFact; partial unique/CHECK constraint on SemanticEdge.object_ref closing PRD risk R-005); Section 3.10 (Zone 3 OWNS: SemanticEdge, GeneralFact; Hard Rule 1: no two zones share a table).

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a candidate fact that spans two or more entities, When it is classified per the Zone 3/Zone 5 ownership ADR (HLD Section 3.4, ADR-006), Then it is stored in Semantic Memory, not duplicated into any single Entity record.

Given a write attempts to persist a SemanticEdge with object_ref IS NULL, When submitted to Zone 3's store, Then the database-level CHECK constraint rejects it, making the R-005 non-duplication regression structurally impossible.

Given a candidate fact with zero subject entity references (|subjects|==0), When classified, Then it is stored as a Zone 3 GeneralFact(tenant_id, fact_id, statement, subject_scope, state, score_terms).
Given a SemanticEdge or GeneralFact record exists in Zone 3, When any other zone's table is inspected, Then no other zone holds a table for these record types, per HLD Section 3.10 Hard Rule 1.

sub_tasks.description: Implement SemanticEdge/GeneralFact schema, DB CHECK/partial-unique constraint on object_ref, Zone 3 storage adapter.
Test constraint rejection, GeneralFact routing for |subjects|==0, and cross-zone table-ownership assertion.
Review that the non-duplication guarantee is DB-level, not application-review-level, per HLD's explicit intent.

must_not_deviate: SemanticEdge and GeneralFact are the only two owned entity types for Zone 3 per HLD Section 3.4/3.10 - no additional owned entity types.
object_ref NOT NULL must be enforced as a DB CHECK/partial-unique constraint, not an application-level convention.
Depends only on DASH-STORY-001 - no zone-to-zone dependency introduced, per HLD Section 3.11 (zones are leaves by design).

acceptance_criteria.text: Facts with |subjects|>1 route to Zone 3 as one SemanticEdge per (subject,object) pair; facts with |subjects|==0 route to Zone 3 as a GeneralFact, per HLD Section 3.4's routing table.

Given |subjects|==1 and |objects|==0 (HLD line 239-240, 'ONLY Zone 5'), no SemanticEdge or GeneralFact write to Zone 3 occurs for any index_reverse value; the paired Zone 5 write stays out of this story's build scope pending FR-005.

sub_tasks.description: Implement EntityOwnershipSpecification classification gate for the |subjects|==0, |subjects|>1, and conditional |subjects|==1 index_reverse=true sub-branch.
Test AC-003-CLASS-1..4 including the index_reverse default-false and true cases.
Review that no Zone 5 attribute write is stubbed or faked, and index_reverse defaults to false.

index_reverse MUST default to false per HLD Section 3.4.

sprint_2_stories.title: Zone 3 to Zone 6 retrieval-index projection (async event emission only)
sprint_2_stories.hld_citation: HLD Section 3.10 (Zone 3 PROJECTS INTO Zone 6); Section 3.7 line 279 (Zone 6 outage is a recall degradation, not a data-loss event, OAQ-16); Section 3.11 (zones are leaves by design).

acceptance_criteria.text: Given a SemanticEdge or GeneralFact is durably written to Zone 3, a projection event is published to the EventBus for Zone 6's index worker to consume.
Zone 3 makes no synchronous call into Zone 6 and carries no recorded dependency on it, per HLD Section 3.11.

When Zone 3 cannot publish a projection event (EventBus unavailable), the underlying durable write is NOT rolled back or rejected, per HLD Section 3.7's 'recall degradation, not a data-loss event' framing (OAQ-16).

sub_tasks.description: Wire Zone 3 write-commit to EventBus projection-event publish for Zone 6 consumption.
Test async, non-blocking publish and write-durability independence from EventBus availability.
Review no synchronous Zone 6 dependency was introduced.

sprint_2_stories.sub_task_sp_note: Sum 4 vs parent 3 - within +/-1 Fibonacci-rounding tolerance per scrum-framework-core Operating Rule 14.

Must not modify Zone 6's consumer/indexing logic (DASH-STORY-007's scope, Hard Rule 1: no two zones share a table).
Zone 3's own write-path durability must remain independent of EventBus/Zone 6 availability.

sprint_2_stories.title: Zone 4 (Procedural) capacity cap and MaxAge rotation backstop wiring
sprint_2_stories.hld_citation: HLD Section 12 rotation-parameters table (Zone 4 row: half-life 120 days, decay constant ~6.68e-8, capacity cap 50,000, MaxAge 730 days, weekly-batch sweep); Section 12C; Section 12F (stops at Compressed while Zone 8 absent).

acceptance_criteria.text: When Zone 4 reaches its capacity cap (50,000) or an item exceeds MaxAge (730 days) in Compressed, the backstop sweep forcibly evicts the lowest-ranked-by-MemoryScore Procedure(s), mirroring the Zone 2 backstop pattern.
A Procedure crossing CompressThreshold (not ArchiveThreshold) transitions to Compressed using a Recency half-life of 120 days.
While Zone 8 is absent, an item that would otherwise cross ArchiveThreshold remains in Compressed indefinitely, bounded only by this story's capacity/MaxAge backstop, per HLD Section 12F.
Capacity cap and MaxAge are deployment configuration; changing either takes effect on the next sweep without a code change.

sub_tasks.description: Wire Zone 4's capacity/MaxAge parameters and eviction predicate into the existing deadline-scheduled sweep engine (DASH-STORY-009).
Test capacity-cap trigger, MaxAge trigger, and Compressed-indefinite-dwell behavior.
Review that no code path attempts an Archived transition for Zone 4 in this story.

sprint_2_stories.sub_task_sp_note: Sum 4 vs parent 3 - within +/-1 Fibonacci-rounding tolerance per scrum-framework-core Operating Rule 14.
must_not_deviate: Do not specify or implement 'step-sequence generalization' (Section 12 rotation table, named once, undefined) as the Compressed-state transform - raise as an open question for the Solution Architect instead.
Do not assume Zone 4 reaches Archived in this story - design stops at Compressed while Zone 8 is absent (Section 12F).
Do not duplicate the generic deadline-scheduled sweep engine (Section 12C) built in DASH-STORY-009 - wire into it, do not reimplement it.

sprint_2_stories.title: Entity Memory zone (Zone 5) - canonical per-entity attribute store with sub-record provenance and alias Trie resolution
sprint_2_stories.hld_citation: HLD Section 3.6 (Zone 5 Entity Memory), cross-referenced with Section 3.10 (Data Ownership Map), Section 3.11 (Dependency Matrix), and DASH-STORY-006/AC-010 (FR-010 write-path rejection contract).

acceptance_criteria.text: Zone 5 returns an EntityRecord by exact (tenant_id, entity_id) via O(1) point lookup.
A single attribute update writes exactly one new provenance record for that attribute only; no sibling attribute's value/provenance_id/updated_at changes; no whole-record rewrite occurs.
Alias prefix resolution returns matching entity_id(s) via Trie prefix match, empty set (not error) when no match.
Exact entity-name/exact-term queries are answered directly by Zone 5's own mechanism even with Zone 6 unavailable, demonstrating the deliberately-not-vector-primary design as observable behavior.
A write attempting to persist an EntityRecord attribute without its own provenance_id is rejected using the same rejection contract DASH-STORY-006/AC-010 established (HTTP 422).
On write commit, a projection event is published to the EventBus for future Zone 6 indexing, asynchronously and non-blocking.

sub_tasks.description: Implement Zone 5 EntityRecord store, point lookup, alias Trie, sub-record provenance write path, ownership-violation rejection gate, projection-event publish.
Test AC-005-1..6, including Zone-6-unavailable exact-query resolution and sibling-attribute-timestamp invariance.
Review reuse of DASH-STORY-006/AC-010's 422 rejection contract and add a QA follow-up item confirming that contract extends correctly to Zone 5.

must_not_deviate: Do NOT implement the Zone 3/Zone 5 write-conflict-detection sweep (HLD Section 3.8) - tracked separately as FR-013, hard-gated behind FR-003 and FR-005 both existing.
Do NOT make Zone 5 vector-primary or route its dominant exact-term query through Zone 6 - must be demonstrated with Zone 6 unavailable.
Do NOT allow any other zone to copy an entity attribute value directly - cross-zone references to Zone 5 use entity_id only.
Do NOT perform a whole-record rewrite on a single-attribute update.
Do NOT build any Zone 6 indexing/consumption logic in this story - only emit the projection event.
Do NOT invent a Zone-5-specific rejection error code - reuse DASH-STORY-006/AC-010's HTTP 422 contract.

sprint_2_stories.title: Zone 8 Consolidation store - object-store blobs with hot manifest index (ADR-009)
sprint_2_stories.hld_citation: HLD Section 3.9 (Zone 8 responsibility, ConsolidatedBlob); ADR-009 Section 4 (storage adapter decision); Section 3.10 (RECEIVES rule, Hard Rule 1); Section 3.11 (zones are leaves); Section 10 threat I-5; Section 8.4 failure-mode table.

acceptance_criteria.text: Manifest resolves item_id -> (blob_id, byte_range, compression_generation) via a single indexed manifest-table lookup plus at most one ranged GET, no full-bucket or full-manifest scan.
Zone 8 accepts writes only as archived items originating from Zone 2, 3, 4 or 5; rejects writes originating directly from Zone 1 or from Zone 6/7, per Section 3.10's RECEIVES rule.
A consolidation merge batch spanning more than one tenant_id fails that batch rather than completing a cross-tenant merge, per threat I-5.
When the object store is unavailable, an archive transition defers (item stays Compressed, no loss/partial write); reads of already-archived items fail 503 scoped only to affected items.

sub_tasks.description: Implement object-store adapter (ADR-009), hot PostgreSQL manifest index, tenant-uniformity merge assertion, degraded-mode handling.
Test manifest resolution, RECEIVES-rule enforcement (against Zone 2, the only available source at ship time), tenant-uniformity failure, and degraded-mode behavior.
Security review of tenant isolation on the consolidation merge path.

must_not_deviate: Zone 8 is reachable only via the Archived state and is never a competing zone to Zones 2-5.
The object-store + hot-manifest shape is locked by ADR-009 (APPROVED) - do not re-open it as a design choice.
Blobs are immutable and content-addressed - never overwritten.
Zone 8 owns ConsolidatedBlob and no other table may duplicate it, per Hard Rule 1.
PM note: only Zone 2 exists as a rotation source at ship time; re-test AC-008-2 against Zones 3/4/5 as each ships.

sprint_2_stories.title: Compressed to Archived rotation transition completion (closes the gap DASH-STORY-009 deliberately deferred)
sprint_2_stories.hld_citation: HLD Section 12A per-zone policy table (Zone 8 row: t_half=270 days, weekly-batch sweep); Section 12B.2-12B.3 (ArchiveThreshold=0.25 derivation); OAQ-1/OAQ-12; Section 12C/ADR-012.

acceptance_criteria.text: A Compressed item crossing ArchiveThreshold (0.25) transitions to Archived and is persisted into Zone 8 as a ConsolidatedBlob with a resolvable manifest entry, completing DASH-STORY-009's AC-012-ROT-1-deferred transition.
An item with payload_tokens < 64 is fast-tracked through Compressed and Archived within the same sweep, per OAQ-12.
All eligible Compressed items are consolidated in a single weekly batch window, no individual per-item archive call outside the batch (other than the OAQ-12 fast-track).
The Archived-transition decision uses the post-mutation, non-stale rotation deadline from DASH-STORY-010's deadline-invalidation wiring, not a cached pre-mutation value.

sub_tasks.description: Implement the Compressed->Archived transition on the existing rotation sweep, OAQ-12 fast-track, and weekly batch cadence.
Test AC-008-ROT-1..4 including the post-mutation deadline read.
Review ArchiveThreshold stays fixed at 0.25 and the PromoteThreshold>CompressThreshold>ArchiveThreshold gating is not reopened.

must_not_deviate: ArchiveThreshold is fixed at 0.25, not the research brief's provisional 0.15 (structurally unreachable per Section 12B.2).
An item SHALL NOT reach Archived without having passed through Compressed.
The OAQ-12 fast-track is gated strictly by payload_tokens < 64, not by score-collapse velocity.
DASH-STORY-004's Zone-2-only capacity/MaxAge backstop must not be left as the sole bound on Compressed growth once this story ships - Zone 8 becomes the real destination.

sprint_2_stories.title: DPDP erasure-cascade reach into Zone 8 archives + India residency and crypto-shredding (ADR-009 India Layer, Section 10 DPDP-2/DPDP-3/DPDP-4)
sprint_2_stories.hld_citation: HLD Section 7.4 (DELETE /v1/tenants/{id}/subjects/{subject_id}); Section 10 DPDP-2/DPDP-3/DPDP-4; ADR-009 India Layer; Section 3.10 (subject_id secondary index, ADR-006); OAQ-10.

acceptance_criteria.text: A DPDP subject-erasure request's cascade reaches Zone 8 archives via the subject_id secondary index (ADR-006), returning 202 with a job_id per the async admin-job pattern.
Each tenant's Zone 8 bucket is provisioned in-region per that tenant's embedding_residency policy, versioned, and object-locked for an operator-configurable audit-retention window.
acceptance_criteria.source: [DERIVED FROM ADR-009 India Layer / Section 10 DPDP-4]

acceptance_criteria.text: A Zone 8 blob subject to DPDP erasure has its per-subject encryption key individually destroyable (crypto-shredding) so the blob becomes permanently unreadable, without an in-place rewrite of the immutable blob.

sub_tasks.description: Implement per-subject key generation/storage/destruction, blob-read-path key integration, in-region versioned/object-locked bucket provisioning, cascade endpoint hook.
Test cascade reach, residency/versioning/object-lock configuration, and post-key-destruction read failure with no blob rewrite issued.
Review that OAQ-10's legal-sufficiency question on crypto-shredding-as-erasure is preserved as open, not asserted as settled.

OAQ-10's legal question (does crypto-shredding satisfy DPDP Act 2023 erasure) is not settled by this story and must not be asserted as such.
The cascade's reach into Zone 8 depends on the subject_id secondary index (ADR-006) being present on the Zone 8 manifest table - do not ship against a schema lacking it.

sprint_5_stories.title: Full DPDP crypto-shredding erasure cascade: subject_id resolution, per-zone key-destroy wiring, DELETE /tenants/{tenant_id}/subjects/{subject_id}
sprint_5_stories.traces_to_hld: HLD.md Section 10 DPDP-2/DPDP-3, ADR-006, ADR-009, OAQ-10 (unresolved)

invest.independent: Builds on DASH-STORY-020's already-shipped Zone 8 per-subject key primitives and DASH-STORY-020/CrossZoneDpdpErasureCascade's Zone 2/Zone 6 reach; does not require any other Sprint 5 story first.

Corrected 2026-09-22, solution-architect review round 6: this field previously and falsely claimed the endpoint was 'contract-only' and the cascade 'never reaches Zones 1/3/4/5/8' -- both false; see the design doc's Section 1 major correction.

Re-estimated to 8 SP, comparable in shape to DASH-STORY-028's own 8 SP wiring-focused story.
invest.small: Scoped to the erasure cascade and its wiring only -- does not reopen the crypto primitives in zone8_crypto_shredding.py themselves (AES-256-GCM, already shipped and tested), does not modify UnifiedSubjectErasureOrchestrator's existing Zone 3/5/8 legs' own logic, and does not attempt to resolve OAQ-10's legal-sufficiency question, which stays explicitly open.
invest.testable: AC-013's own SRS wording plus the design doc's own Definition-of-Done section give concrete Given-When-Then coverage per zone.

sprint_5_stories.scope_correction_2026_09_22: The linked design doc surfaced a prerequisite finding not known when this story was first drafted: Zones 4 (Procedural) and 5 (Entity) have no Postgres/Shape-B storage adapter at all today (only in-process, non-durable Shape A stores) -- there is nothing durable to erase there in a real deployment. This story's own cascade scope is therefore Zones 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 (the zones with durable storage) plus a forward-compatible interface for Zone 4/5, NOT all 8 zones directly. Zone 4/5 Shape B adapters are tracked as a separate, out-of-scope infrastructure prerequisite (see future_sprints_backlog below) rather than silently assumed complete by this story.
sprint_5_stories.scope_correction_2026_09_22_round6: MAJOR: solution-architect review round 6 found this story's original design doc never read `subject_erasure_cascade.py`, `zone8_crypto_shredding_store.py`, `unified_subject_erasure_orchestrator.py`, or `sql_zone8_subject_index_repository.py` -- all real, already-built prior art from DASH-STORY-020/025. The endpoint IS wired (Zone 8 only, live today); a separate, more complete orchestrator (Zones 2/3/5/6/8) is already built but NOT wired into that endpoint; Zone 1 is genuinely missing from both. This story is RE-SCOPED from 'build the full cascade' to 'wire the existing orchestrator into the live endpoint, implement its already-defined SubjectToItemIndex seam for real, and add the missing Zone 1 leg' -- see the design doc's own Section 1 major correction for full detail. Zone 4 is now known to be PERMANENTLY excluded (no subject-linkable field exists, not merely storage-blocked); Zone 5's real remaining gap is a Shape B adapter only (its erasure LOGIC already works today for Shape A).

acceptance_criteria.text: SRS.md AC-013 (verbatim, see SRS.md for the exact text) -- a subject-scoped erasure request reaches all 8 zones, both retrieval indices, and Zone 8 archives.

Given a DPDP erasure request for subject_id S, When DELETE /tenants/{tenant_id}/subjects/{subject_id} is called, Then every item_id associated with S across Zones 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 (the zones with durable Shape B storage today) is resolved via a real subject_id index and enters the erasure cascade -- via UnifiedSubjectErasureOrchestrator's existing Zone 2/3/5/6/8 fan-out plus this story's own new Zone 1 leg, not a from-scratch cascade -- and the interface is forward-compatible so Zone 4/5 slot in once their own Shape B adapters exist.

Given the review completes, When OAQ-10 (does crypto-shredding legally satisfy DPDP Act erasure) is checked, Then no shipped code, docstring, or API response asserts legal sufficiency -- the question remains explicitly open, carried forward from HLD.md and the design doc unchanged.

sprint_5_stories.story_points_note: RE-ESTIMATED 2026-09-22 (consensus-agent round-3 re-review remediation, item 3 of 4): was 8 SP (5+2+1) under solution-architect review round 6's re-scoping, which covered wiring/extension work only. The design doc's Section 7 durability mechanism (write-ahead marker before the irreversible Zone 8 key-destroy, a finalize step that atomically promotes the marker into the Zone 7 record AND deletes subject_item_index rows, a restart-time recovery sweep that must distinguish CONFIRMED from UNCONFIRMED destruction and act differently for each, bounded k=2/exponential-backoff item-level retry, and a terminal FAILED state with human-compliance-owner escalation) took 3 consensus-agent review rounds to design precisely because it is genuinely new, non-trivial state-machine/recovery logic -- not an incremental addition to the wiring work already scoped. Judged a meaningful chunk of new work, not covered by the original 8 SP. Bumped to the next Fibonacci value per this file's own estimation_method (Fibonacci {1,2,3,5,8,13}, 70/20/10 Dev/QA/Review split, +/-1 SP sub-task tolerance): 13 SP, split 9/3/1. Review's own SP is unchanged from the original 1 -- AC-027-REVIEW-2/3/4 already require auditing the shipped mechanism's behavior, not designing or building it, so the review's scope (audit, not construction) does not grow proportionally with Dev/QA's.

sub_tasks.description: Wire the already-built UnifiedSubjectErasureOrchestrator into app.py's eraseSubject handler (replacing/extending the narrower Zone-8-only SubjectErasureCascadeService call); implement a real SubjectToItemIndex (Shape B Postgres subject-index table, with per-zone row cleanup after successful erasure) fulfilling the orchestrator's already-defined Protocol seam; add a Zone 1 leg to the orchestrator (genuinely missing today); a compliance-role DELETE adapter for Zone 2 ONLY (implementing the existing Zone2EvictionPort Protocol -- Zone 1 is an ordinary hot-buffer evict and Zone 3 has no append-only trigger, so neither needs one, per the design doc's Section 4 zone-by-zone table). Re-scoped 2026-09-22 per solution-architect review round 6 -- was 'build the full cascade from scratch', corrected to 'wire and extend the already-built orchestrator'. acceptance_criteria.text: Given the API host is under concurrent load, When multiple requests touch different zones' SQL repositories simultaneously, Then each acquires its own pooled connection rather than contending on one shared psycopg.Connection object.

Given the pool is exhausted under load, When a new request needs a connection, Then the API returns 503 + Retry-After, consistent with the existing NFR-014/AC-021 contention-handling pattern, rather than blocking indefinitely or crashing.

Given the change lands, When any existing zone repository's own code is inspected, Then it is unchanged -- it still depends only on the SqlConnection Protocol; only the composition root's acquisition/release mechanics change.

Given repeated Postgres connect/acquire failures, When the failure/slow-connect thresholds are crossed, Then a circuit breaker trips OPEN and fails fast (503+Retry-After) without attempting pool acquisition, transitions to HALF_OPEN after a backoff period, and closes only when its probe attempts all succeed -- mirroring HLD.md Section 8's existing vector-store breaker pattern and reusing HLD.md Section 5's existing ring-buffer breaker utility rather than a new mechanism.

Scope: real Shape B deployment per HLD Section 2's container/service table (Postgres, Redis, Qdrant, OpenSearch, S3), a real DB driver dependency (pyproject.toml currently declares zero), docker-compose, env config, and a migration runner -- none of which exist anywhere in this repo today (confirmed by direct exploration 2026-09-20: no docker-compose*, no .env*, no settings/config module, no alembic). This is also where the production DB-role-wiring gap closes for real: dashanan_app_role/dashanan_schema_owner (defined in provenance_schema.sql/episodic_schema.sql since DSHN-55) get bound to an actual login credential via this story's connection-string/composition-root wiring, not before. Real dependency on FR-014: a wire layer with no real backing store (Postgres/Redis/etc.) is still Shape-A-only underneath it, so FR-014 alone does not make the system meaningfully production-deployable without FR-015. User-directed scoping (2026-09-20): candidate for the same future sprint wave as FR-014, per explicit preference for combining them rather than sequencing across separate sprints.

dependency_graph.promotion_reason: DASH-STORY-002 (Working Memory, Zone 1) is the sole root dependency for DASH-STORY-005 (Zone 7) per the mandated dependency graph. DASH-STORY-007 (Zone 6) depends on DASH-STORY-003 (Zone 2), corrected per SP.0.5 SA review C-3: Zone 6 indexes Zones 2-5, 7, 8 and explicitly not Zone 1 (HLD Section 3.7), so Zone 6's real content dependency is Zone 2, not Zone 1. sprint_2_dependency_graph.promotion_reason: All Sprint 2 zone-store stories (DASH-STORY-012, -015, -017, -018) depend only on DASH-STORY-001 (Orchestrator facade), consistent with Sprint 1's promotion_reason that every write/read routes through the facade and zones are leaves by design (HLD Section 3.11). DASH-STORY-013 and DASH-STORY-014 depend on their own zone's store (DASH-STORY-012) landing first, plus DASH-STORY-007 (Zone 6) for the projection story. DASH-STORY-016 (Zone 4 backstop) depends on DASH-STORY-008 (MemoryScore engine) and DASH-STORY-009 (rotation state machine) exactly as DASH-STORY-004 (the Zone 2 analogue) did in Sprint 1. DASH-STORY-019 and DASH-STORY-020 depend on DASH-STORY-018 (Zone 8 store) landing first, since both extend the store's write path (rotation completion and DPDP cascade respectively).

sprint_5_dependency_graph.promotion_reason: DASH-STORY-027 (full DPDP erasure cascade) depends on DASH-STORY-020 (Sprint 2's narrower Shape A crypto-shredding/Zone-8-reach mechanism) AND DASH-STORY-025 (already-shipped UnifiedSubjectErasureOrchestrator fan-out, added 2026-09-22 per solution-architect review round 6 -- this story wires/extends that orchestrator rather than building a new cascade from scratch).
